title: Divis Laboratories Ltd - 532488 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Divi's Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose to ₹891 crores (from ₹557 crores), with Custom Synthesis at 60% of revenue and management guiding to double-digit growth.
summary.overview: Consolidated total income was ₹3,144 crores versus ₹2,529 crores a year earlier, and consolidated PAT was ₹902 crores versus ₹545 crores. Standalone revenue grew 10% in constant currency, with Custom Synthesis at 60% and Generics at 40% of revenue. Gross margin and inventory build were the main swing factors: the company stocked solvents and raw materials on a rolling three-month basis at higher cost and also built validation-batch inventory, and management said margins should be read on a full-year basis. Management declined to quantify commercial ramp-up timelines for the three capex projects, citing CDAs and regulatory timing.

segments.name: Custom Synthesis
segments.commentary: Contributed 60% of standalone revenue in Q1 FY27. Three major capex projects are in validation and about 70% of their combined ~₹2,000 crore cost has been capitalised. Management said the company has about 18 to 20 projects commercialised or being commercialised.

segments.name: Generics
segments.commentary: Contributed 40% of standalone revenue. Volumes were stable and pricing reflected competitive conditions; management said about 4 DMFs have been filed, with Brivaracetam and Ticagrelor under customer qualification and commercial volumes expected in 3 to 6 months after qualification.

segments.name: Nutraceuticals
segments.commentary: Revenue of ₹298 crores versus ₹250 crores a year earlier, and about ₹240 crores in Q4 FY26 per analyst. Portfolio is over 100 offerings, and the company is expanding capabilities and capacity.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated double-digit revenue growth for FY27 and said it would show double-digit growth 'no matter what'; it did not give a specific gross or EBITDA margin figure.
Management said full-year gross margin is about 60% and EBITDA margin is similar to last year, but Q1 gross margin was about 68% and the company does not expect that level to persist.

Commercial volumes from the validated capex projects depend on customer qualification and agency approvals; no firm timing was given beyond the 'later part of the current financial year' referenced in analyst questions.
Iodine-based contrast media: long-term contracts being signed with two customers; one has started commercialisation and the second is expected to start in the next few months.
Gadolinium contrast media remains in Phase II/III customer qualification, with the customer awaiting regulatory approvals.
capex_capacity: Three major capex projects are nearing completion with validations ongoing; about ₹2,000 crores in total and about 70% capitalised so far.
Capitalised assets during Q1 were ₹451 crores; capital work in progress was ₹2,034 crores as of June 30, 2026.
Utilisation across Units 1, 2 and 3 is about 80% to 85% (CFO said ~85% across all three units).

Unit 3 at Kakinada is being used for pre-chemistry and backward-integrated work; the company is filling it with pre-chemistry products while regulatory qualification of the plant, which could take 1 to 2 years, is pursued.
Peptides: expanding solid-phase and liquid-phase peptide synthesis, including acquiring several additional 3,000-litre SPPS units.
demand_pricing: Solvent costs rose sharply, with some solvents nearly doubling or tripling in price due to West Asia disruption; the company passed through some costs and raised prices slightly where possible.
Management attributed generic price increases to raw material cost pass-through rather than a durable end of pricing pressure.
Freight rates remained elevated, and ocean and air logistics faced port congestion, blank sailings and longer transit times.
Exports were about 90% of standalone revenue; Europe and North America were 75% of exports.
Management declined to name competitors and said Divi's differentiates through full backward integration from raw materials, in-house resins and protected amino acids.

qa_highlights.question: What is the typical ramp from validation quantities to commercial quantities for dedicated capex projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify, citing CDAs and product-specific variability. Commercial volumes start only after validation, customer qualification and agency approval.

qa_highlights.question: Will the inventory build (≈₹500 crores change in inventory) normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: The company is holding a rolling three-month stock of materials at higher cost to avoid production or shipment stoppages, and validation batches also add to inventory. Management said the inventory level depends on Middle East macro conditions and would fall if costs normalise.

qa_highlights.question: How should full-year margins compare with last year?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-year gross margin is about 60% and EBITDA margin is similar to last year, with lumpiness by quarter. Q1 gross margin was about 68% and the next quarter may be higher or lower.

qa_highlights.question: Is solvent pricing softening?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said prices were flat for a few weeks and then rose again depending on Middle East news. Supply is not always easily available, so the company is holding inventory three months ahead rather than just-in-time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Gadolinium contrast media project?
qa_highlights.answer: It is still in customer Phase II and III qualification and is on a slow track while the customer awaits regulatory approval. Validation has not yet been completed.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any inventory gain in the gross margin line this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: No, management said there was no inventory gain recorded in Q1.

risks_watch: Solvent and raw material cost volatility tied to West Asia; prices can rise again within weeks, and the 3-month inventory policy ties up working capital (inventory ₹4,413 crores).
Timing of regulatory approvals (FDA and other agencies) for the three capex projects and the Brivaracetam/Ticagrelor DMFs; approvals drive the Custom Synthesis mix shift.
Gross margin normalisation after Q1's approximately 68% level, and the inventory-change swing from roughly ₹50-100 crores run rate to about ₹500 crores.
Net forex loss of ₹7 crores in Q1 versus a gain of ₹39 crores a year earlier; INR movements affect reported margins.
Freight and logistics disruption affecting export schedules, and the need to watch validation-to-commercial conversion for the Kakinada Unit 3 site.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and the double-digit growth outlook, but cautious and often evasive on quantities, timelines and margins, citing CDA confidentiality, regulatory uncertainty and Middle East volatility.
key_quotes: I would like to stick to my statement saying that we will show double -digit growth no matter what.
And these we are securing at a higher cost to make sure there is no production stoppage and there is no shipments that are delayed to our customers.
So whatever you're seeing right now is a market correction based on the raw material prices that have taken a substantial hit.
We would say, if you want to look at a revenue projection, we are looking at double-digit growth.

Unit 3 Kakinada pre-chemistry / backward-integrated work; regulatory qualification of plant could take 1-2 years
Additional 3,000-litre SPPS peptide synthesis units (number not stated)

growth.why: Management reaffirmed double-digit FY27 revenue growth ("for sure", "no matter what") with no numeric margin target, backed partly by three ~₹2,000 crore Custom Synthesis projects nearing completion (~70% capitalised, validations ongoing, no firm commercial timing), iodine contrast contracts with two customers, and Generics DMFs under qualification.
